syllabus_extract: Definition of Prepregs. Application of prepregs in aerospace industry. Advantages and disadvantages of prepress. Storage of Prepregs.
specific_objectives: 17.1.1.1 Trainee will be able to understand the development of composite materials, types and functions of fibers and resin, Defects in composite, selection criteria for Matrix, fabric weaves, prepress, strength flowcharts

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of prepreg storage conditions and handling safety precautions; Instructor supervision required for safety compliance.
intro_questions: What are the primary components of a composite material?
Why are composite materials preferred over conventional metals in aerospace?
Can you define the term 'prepreg' based on your prior knowledge?

topics: Functions of fibers and resin systems
development.content:
Definition and composition of prepregs
Development history of composite materials
Functions of fibers and resin systems
Fabric weaves and selection criteria
Matrix selection parameters

Applications in aerospace industry
Advantages of prepreg technology
Disadvantages and limitations
Common defects in composite structures
Strength flowcharts and performance metrics

Storage requirements for prepregs
Temperature and humidity control
Shelf life management
Handling and cutting procedures
Safety precautions during storage

summary_questions: Explain the critical difference between wet layup and prepreg manufacturing methods.
List three specific advantages of using prepregs in aerospace structural applications.
Describe the storage conditions required to maintain prepreg integrity.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief report comparing the stress-strain characteristics of composite prepregs versus conventional metals, referencing the data to be covered in LP 06.

pft_rows.syllabus: Comparison of composite with conventional metal w.r.t stress-strain graphical diagram.
